assumptions: Both buildings are assigned to the existing traced roof proxies and their plaza-facing western edges. Roof displacement and 5 m assumed georeferencing uncertainty remain; the assignment is adopted, not surveyed.
Existing 20 m / 28 m proxy roof heights remain assumed total masses. Lower frontage, tower setback, door/window modules and steps are construction choices informed by photographs.
Pale neutral mineral wall colours, dark metal and green-grey glazing are selected for a coherent full-colour reconstruction. Black-and-white photographs do not prove these colours.
Fountain shape and location are inferred from the aerial; dimensions and lamp positions remain modeling assumptions. The three lamp positions are not claimed as measured historical pole positions.
Use stable building names and neutral poster panels. No actual programme, event, or exact day in 1976 is invented.
Current DEM supplies a continuous ground datum. It is a modern terrain reference rather than a verified 1976 pavement elevation.
The seven-globe count and crown dimensions are an adopted procedural simplification of the multi-globe lamp style; no exact pole inventory or measured globe count is claimed.
Toho canopy underside is adopted at 4.15 m above plaza grade so the 1.2 m stair rise and 2.7 m door opening do not intersect it; Plaza lettering baseline 4.55 m is an authored placement.
After fitting actual CJK glyph bounds, the Plaza Theatre lettering centre stays at 4.95 m so its 0.85 m glyph bounds clear the Toho canopy top; this is an authored layout dimension.

r05: the two Koma canopy names stand on the canopy top (glyph centre 3.895 m = 3.1 m underside + 0.22 m slab + 0.15 m rail + half of 0.85 m) following the 1957 mounting motif; carrying that mounting to 1976 is an assumption.

r05: two lamp positions moved by one or two aerial pixels (about 1.9 m and 1.0 m), inside the recorded 2 m prop-placement uncertainty, so that no pole stands in the fixed stations' sightlines to the theatre names. This is a composition-driven placement choice, not new positional evidence.

contradictions.issue: 1957 canopy strings versus the adopted コマ劇場 canopy name (r05 re-inspection)
contradictions.resolution: Unresolved. On re-inspection the 1957 canopy letters read コマ東宝 and, on the second ledge, コマシネマ (r02 transcribed the second as コマ劇場; the r02-listed museum catalogue 5295 title also names コマ東宝 and コマシネマ). The adopted west-front name コマ劇場 is kept as the facility name; no photograph shows that string on the plaza front in 1976.

contradictions.issue: Ring emblem with KOMA lettering in the 1975/1979 plaza photographs (r05 re-inspection)
contradictions.resolution: Unresolved and not changed in r05. The large ring emblem on the white wall right of the stairs carries the latin letters KOMA, a Koma production banner hangs on the same wall and a large latin K follows to the right. This contradicts reading the ring as the Toho Kaikan emblem (r03 parameters emblem_*, placed at 0.78 of the Toho front by the r03 script). Recorded for a separate revision.

contradictions.issue: Vertical order of the Toho front in the 1975/1979 photographs (r05 re-inspection)
contradictions.resolution: Recorded only: the photographs show programme billboards below the プラザ劇場 band and a glazed upper level above it. The r04 viewer's authored billboard above プラザ劇場 is a period-plausible-generic placement, not an adopted value; it is not changed in r05.

evidence.observation: Re-inspected on 2026-11-03 in a web browser from the publisher's reproduction (enlarged on screen; no pixels copied into the repository). The building-name letters are three-dimensional box letters standing on top of the deep canopy and on a ledge further along the front, with a light frame behind them and shadows on the wall; the rooftop name letters stand on the parapet the same way. No name is mounted flush on the wall below the canopy line.

counter_evidence: The 1957 photograph is about 19 years earlier; carrying the mounting to 1976 is an assumption.
The 1957 canopy strings read コマ東宝 and コマシネマ, not コマ劇場 (see contradictions); the adopted name string is a production choice.
The 1975/1979 photographs show a ring emblem with KOMA and large latin letters on the Koma's plaza side, so the 1976 lettering on this side may have differed altogether.
